mainTopic: Whether the Sages make a גזירה לגזירה (כרמלית, the tailor's needle), and when carrying an object like a זב's pouch counts as Torah-level carrying
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה from עירובין: you may not stand in one domain and drink from another unless your head and most of your body are inside, 'and the same is true in the wine press.' The גמרא asks whether this ban also covers a כרמלית. אביי says yes. רבא says no, because we do not make a גזירה לגזירה. אביי tries to prove his view from 'וכן בגת', but רבא and רב ששת read that line as a rule about מעשר, and the tithe משנה about drinking at the press is quoted. The גמרא then tries to support אביי from the ban on a tailor going out with his needle before Shabbat. Each proof is turned away, and the last one is explained as following רבי יהודה, who holds that a craftsman carrying in his trade's usual way is liable. This leads to two contradictory ברייתות about a זב going out with his pouch. רב יוסף's answer that they follow רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה is rejected by אביי. רב המנונא instead distinguishes a זב with two sightings from one with three. רבי זירא defends that answer by saying this תנא does not count preventing dirt as a real purpose, and he begins quoting a משנה about a bowl on a wall, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the quoted source: the same is true in the wine press
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the quoted משנה extend its rule to a wine press.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true in the wine press.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the source the גמרא just quoted. That source says you may not stand in one domain and drink from another unless your head and most of your body are inside, and it adds that the same applies at a wine press. The גמרא is setting up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is short and does not say what kind of domain a wine press is. That unclear point becomes the center of the argument between אביי and רבא below.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine press, a pit or vat where grapes are pressed
And likewise, the same applies

phrases.english: And the same is true in the wine press.
phrases.notes: This is where the quote from the משנה in עירובין ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source quoted on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule against drinking across domains (unless head and most of the body are inside) also applies at a wine press.

steps.title: What about a כרמלית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ban on drinking across domains also applies to a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law regarding a כרמלית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. Does the rule against drinking from another domain also apply when one of the places is a כרמלית?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source clearly covers the two Torah-level domains, רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים. A כרמלית is a middle domain created by the rabbis, so it is unclear whether the same ban applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the scholars)
An in-between domain on Shabbat, not fully private or public, created by the rabbis
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What about a karmelit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the rule in the quoted source reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ban on drinking from one domain while standing in another also applies to a כרמלית.

steps.title: אביי: the same rule applies
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a כרמלית is treated the same as the other domains.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. A כרמלית works just like the other domains, so drinking across it is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the rabbis' worry applies the same way everywhere. The worry is that a person might bring the drink over to himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the same thing (the same law)

phrases.english: Abaye said: it is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כרמלית is forbidden just like the other domains.

steps.title: רבא: no decree on top of a decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits it with a כרמלית, because that would be stacking a rabbinic decree on another rabbinic decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the כרמלית itself is only a rabbinic decree. Should we then go and make a decree to protect a decree?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with אביי. He says drinking across from a כרמלית is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on drinking across domains is itself only a protective fence, made in case the person carries the drink across. Carrying to or from a כרמלית is already forbidden only by the rabbis. Adding a fence to protect a rabbinic rule would be a גזירה לגזירה, which the rabbis do not do.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to protect against breaking a law
A decree made to protect another decree, which is generally not done
It itself

steps.whatToRemember: The argument comes down to one idea. אביי treats a כרמלית like any other domain, while רבא says we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It itself (karmelit) is a decree,
and shall we arise and decree
a decree for a decree?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; he means 'surely not!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כרמלית is not included, because we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: אביי's proof from the wine press
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the wine press in the source must be a כרמלית, which shows the ban applies there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: how do I know this? Because it teaches 'and the same is true in the wine press.' What kind of place is the wine press? If it is a רשות היחיד, that was already taught. If it is a רשות הרבים, that was already taught too. So it must be a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof for his view from the words 'וכן בגת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source already covered רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים. Adding the wine press would teach nothing new unless the press is a different kind of domain, namely a כרמלית. That shows the ban includes a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it (what is my source)?
We have already learned it (so why repeat it?)
Rather, is it not that...?
Private domain
Public domain

phrases.english: Abaye said: from where do I say it?
For it teaches: 'And the same is true in the wine press.'
What is the wine press?
If it is a private domain, we already learned it!
If it is a public domain, we already learned it.
Rather, is it not a karmelit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in step 3 using the source in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that the ban applies to a כרמלית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'וכן בגת' in the quoted source, which would add nothing unless they refer to a כרמלית.

steps.title: רבא: the wine press clause is about tithes
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof by reading 'וכן בגת' as a rule about מעשר, not Shabbat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'and the same is true in the wine press' is about tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's proof. The wine press line has nothing to do with Shabbat domains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'וכן בגת' is about מעשר, then it says nothing about a כרמלית, and אביי's proof falls apart. On this reading, a person may drink at the press without tithing, as casual drinking, only if his head and most of his body are inside the press.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding the matter of
Tithe, the portion of produce that must be separated

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying a wine press is not a domain. He is only saying this particular line in the source is teaching a law about מעשר rather than a Shabbat law.

phrases.english: Rava said:
'And the same is true in the wine press' refers to tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: וְכֵן בַּגַּת לְעִנְיַן מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, by reinterpreting the clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי assumed 'וכן בגת' is about Shabbat domains, but it can be read as a rule about מעשר.

steps.title: רב ששת agrees: the clause is about tithes
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives the same reading as רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רב ששת said: 'and the same is true in the wine press' is about tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that another sage, רב ששת, read the line the same way as רבא. It is setting up the quote of the tithe source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a second authority give the same reading makes רבא's rejection stronger. It shows the tithe reading is not an invention made just to escape אביי's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too said (introduces agreement)

phrases.english: And so too Rav Sheshet said:
'And the same is true in the wine press' refers to tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבא's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'וכן בגת' refers to the laws of מעשר.

steps.title: The tithe source: רבי מאיר exempts drinking at the press
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה showing there are tithe laws about drinking at the wine press.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one may drink at the wine press, whether the wine is mixed with hot water or with cold water, and he is exempt from tithing. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה about מעשר to show that drinking at the press is a known topic in tithe law. רבי מאיר says it is exempt either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before tithes are separated, one may eat or drink casually, but not as a fixed meal. רבי מאיר treats drinking at the press as casual drinking in both cases, so no tithe is required.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Hot (water mixed into the wine)
Cold (water mixed into the wine)
Exempt

phrases.english: As we learned: one may drink at the wine press,
whether with hot water,
or with cold water, and he is exempt.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the tithe source behind רבא's and רב ששת's reading.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that 'וכן בגת' concerns מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about drinking at the press without tithing.

steps.title: The other opinions: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק and the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק requires tithing in both cases. The חכמים require it with hot water but exempt it with cold water, because the leftover can be poured back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק requires tithing. The חכמים say: with hot water he must tithe. With cold water he is exempt, because he pours the leftover back into the press.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה finishes with two more opinions about drinking at the press. This completes the tithe source that רבא and רב ששת rely on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים look at whether the leftover wine can go back into the press. With cold water it can be poured back, so the drinking stays casual and is exempt. Leftover wine mixed with hot water would spoil the press, so it cannot go back. That makes the drinking like a fixed drink, which requires tithing.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires (tithing); holds one obligated
Obligated
He returns the leftover (to the press)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads 'וכן בגת' as a tithe rule, so it gives no proof for אביי that a כרמלית is included in the Shabbat ban.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok obligates (tithing).
And the Sages say:
With hot water, he is obligated.
With cold water, he is exempt,
because he returns the leftover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted tithe משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק requires tithing in both cases. The חכמים require it with hot water and exempt it with cold water, since the leftover can be returned to the press.

steps.title: Proof from the tailor's needle in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה about a חייט and his מחט near nightfall to support אביי's idea of a decree on top of a decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: A tailor should not go out with his needle close to nightfall, in case he forgets and goes out with it after Shabbat starts. Isn't this talking about a needle stuck in his clothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove אביי right from a משנה. It suggests that the needle in the משנה was stuck in the tailor's clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a needle stuck in your clothes is not the normal way of carrying, so on Shabbat it is only a rabbinic ban. If the Sages still banned going out with it before Shabbat, they added a decree to protect another decree. That is a גזירה לגזירה, which would support אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Tailor
Needle
Close to nightfall, just before Shabbat
Stuck into, pinned in
A protective decree made to guard another decree

steps.confusionAlert: The tailor is not being stopped from carrying on Shabbat itself here. He is being stopped from going out before Shabbat, in case he forgets the needle is on him once Shabbat begins.

phrases.english: We learned: The tailor may not go out with his needle
close to nightfall (on Friday)
in case he forgets and goes out (after Shabbat starts).
Is it not talking about a needle stuck in his clothing?
phrases.notes: If so, carrying it on Shabbat is only rabbinic, and the ban before Shabbat is a decree on top of a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּיט בְּמַחֲטוֹ סָמוּךְ לַחֲשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new attempt to support אביי's approach, after the wine press proof was turned away.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that the Sages add a decree to protect another rabbinic decree
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a tailor may not go out with his needle close to nightfall

steps.title: No, he is holding the needle in his hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה is talking about holding the needle in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about where he is holding it in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the משנה could be about a needle held in the hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying something in your hand is the normal way of carrying, so on Shabbat that is a Torah-level violation. The ban before Shabbat then protects a Torah law, which is just one decree. There is no decree on top of a decree, so there is no proof for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Holding
In his hand

phrases.english: No, it is where he holds it in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 10 by giving the case a different setting.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the needle was stuck in his clothing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be about a needle held in the hand, which is Torah-level carrying. So no decree on top of a decree is needed.

steps.title: Proof from a teaching that says 'stuck in his clothing'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא openly says the needle is stuck in his clothing. The גמרא suggests it is talking about ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A tailor may not go out with his needle stuck in his clothing. Isn't that talking about Friday afternoon?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that clearly says the needle is stuck in the clothing. It suggests this ban is about ערב שבת, which would again support אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the 'held in his hand' answer from step 11 cannot work, because the text clearly says 'stuck in his clothing.' If this ban is about Friday, it is a decree before Shabbat that protects a rabbinic ban. That would be a גזירה לגזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which brings a new proof
Friday, before Shabbat starts

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּיט בְּמַחֲטוֹ
phrases.english: Come and hear: The tailor may not go out with his needle
that is stuck in his clothing.
Is it not talking about Friday (before Shabbat)?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּיט בְּמַחֲטוֹ הַתְּחוּבָה לוֹ בְּבִגְדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 11 by using a source that clearly says the needle was stuck in his clothing.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that the Sages make a decree on top of a decree
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a tailor may not go out with his needle stuck in his clothing

steps.title: No, that teaching is about Shabbat itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this ברייתא is about going out on Shabbat itself, not on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, when that was taught, it was about Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns away the proof again. It says the ברייתא is talking about going out on Shabbat day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going out on Shabbat with a needle stuck in your clothes is a simple rabbinic ban. It is only one decree, with no extra decree added on top. So there is no proof for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: When that teaching was taught

phrases.english: No, when that was taught, it was about Shabbat itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 12 by changing when the case happens.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as being about ערב שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be about Shabbat day, where the ban is just one rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Proof from a teaching that clearly says Friday at nightfall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that clearly says both 'stuck in his clothing' and 'Friday at nightfall.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: A tailor may not go out with his needle stuck in his clothing on Friday close to nightfall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that blocks both earlier rejections. It clearly says the needle is stuck in the clothing and that the time is ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither 'held in his hand' nor 'on Shabbat itself' can work now. This looks like a clear example of a decree on top of a decree, just as אביי says. The גמרא now has to find a different way to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught, which brings a stronger source
At nightfall

phrases.english: But it was taught: The tailor may not go out with his needle
that is stuck in his clothing
on Friday at nightfall.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּיט בְּמַחֲטוֹ הַתְּחוּבָה בְּבִגְדוֹ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עִם חֲשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks both earlier rejections at the same time with a clearly worded source.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that the Sages make a decree on top of a decree
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that mentions both 'stuck in his clothing' and 'ערב שבת at nightfall'

steps.title: That teaching follows רבי יהודה's view about craftsmen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds that an אומן carrying in his work's usual way is liable by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is this teaching from? It is רבי יהודה, who said: a craftsman carrying in the way of his craft is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the strong proof by saying the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. For a tailor, a needle in his clothes is the normal way to carry it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, a tailor carrying his needle stuck in his clothes breaks a Torah law on Shabbat. So the ban before Shabbat protects a Torah law, and it is only one decree. אביי's idea of a decree on top of a decree is still not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Craftsman, a worker with a trade
The usual way of his trade
Liable, meaning he broke a Torah law

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: whether carrying is 'normal' can depend on the person. What is unusual for most people can be normal for a worker in his trade.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: a craftsman (carrying) in the way of his craft is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 14 by saying the ברייתא follows a particular תנא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Accepts that the ברייתא is about Friday and 'stuck in clothing,' but rejects that it shows a decree on top of a decree.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For רבי יהודה, a tailor's needle in his clothing is Torah-level carrying. So the Friday ban is a single decree.

steps.title: The teaching where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about craftsmen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows רבי יהודה's view: several workers carrying their tools in their usual way. רבי מאיר says they are exempt but forbidden, and רבי יהודה says they are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: A tailor may not go out with his needle stuck in his clothing. A carpenter may not go out with the wood chip on his ear. A wool comber may not go out with the cord on his ear. A weaver may not go out with the bit of wool on his ear. A dyer may not go out with the sample on his neck. A money changer may not go out with the coin in his ear. If he went out, he is exempt but it is forbidden. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: a craftsman in the way of his craft is liable, and anyone else is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what it just said about רבי יהודה. It lists several workers who carry their work items in unusual places, and shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that carrying in an unusual place is never a Torah violation, even for a worker. That is only rabbinically forbidden. רבי יהודה holds that for the worker himself, this place is normal, so he is liable by Torah law. Everyone else is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Carpenter
Wood chip, used as a measuring stick
Wool comber
Weaver
Money changer
Exempt from a Torah penalty, but forbidden by the Rabbis

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says a worker carrying his tool in his usual place is exempt but forbidden. רבי יהודה says the worker is liable by Torah law, and only other people are exempt. The tailor-on-Friday ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, so it does not prove a decree on top of a decree.

phrases.english: As it was taught: The tailor may not go out with his needle
that is stuck in his clothing,
nor a carpenter with the wood chip on his ear,
nor a wool comber with the cord on his ear,
nor a weaver with the bit of wool on his ear,
nor a dyer with the color sample on his neck,
nor a money changer with the coin in his ear.
And if he went out, he is exempt, but it is forbidden,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אוּמָּן דֶּרֶךְ אוּמָּנֻתוֹ — חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: a craftsman in the way of his craft is liable,
and every other person is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּיט בְּמַחֲטוֹ הַתְּחוּבָה לוֹ בְּבִגְדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יהודה's view that was used in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds a craftsman carrying in his trade's way is liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing the tailor, carpenter, comber, weaver, dyer, and money changer

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about a זב going out with his pouch
steps.stepSummary: Two ברייתות contradict each other: one says a זב who goes out with his pouch is exempt but it is forbidden, and the other says he must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teaching says: A זב may not go out with his pouch, and if he went out, he is exempt but it is forbidden. Another teaching says: He may not go out, and if he went out, he must bring a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new contradiction between two ברייתות about a זב and his pouch. The answer comes next, so this step is preparing the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both teachings agree the זב may not go out with the pouch from the start. They disagree about what happens if he did: one says no Torah liability, and the other says full Torah liability with a חטאת. This links to the argument just quoted about carrying in an unusual way.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a certain kind of impure bodily discharge
Pouch, worn to catch the discharge
Must bring a sin-offering, meaning he broke a Torah law by accident
Another teaching says

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: לֹא יֵצֵא הַזָּב בְּכִיסוֹ,
phrases.english: One teaching says: A zav may not go out with his pouch,
and if he went out, he is exempt, but it is forbidden.
And another teaching says: He may not go out,
and if he went out, he must bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: לֹא יֵצֵא הַזָּב בְּכִיסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argument about unusual carrying to open a new contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about a זב going out with his pouch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same act gets two opposite rulings: exempt but forbidden, versus liable to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The Two ברייתות Follow Different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the exempt ברייתא follows רבי מאיר and the liable ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי מאיר, and that one follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the contradiction between the two ברייתות about the זב's pouch. He says each one follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the מחלוקת from step 16. רבי מאיר says carrying in a way that is not the object's usual way is פטור אבל אסור, so he matches the 'exempt' ברייתא. רבי יהודה says an אומן carrying in his own usual way is liable, and for a זב this is his usual way of carrying, so he matches the 'חטאת' ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase opens an answer.
This one... that one. It assigns each source to a different case or opinion.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: this one is Rabbi Meir, that one is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two sources to two different תנאים (a מחלוקת תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exempt ruling follows רבי מאיר and the liable ruling follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: אביי: רבי מאיר Only Exempted an Unusual Way of Carrying
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי מאיר exempted only carrying that is not the object's usual way. A זב's pouch is always carried this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Say that you heard רבי מאיר exempt something that is not its usual way of being carried. But did you hear him exempt something that is its usual way?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer. He says רבי מאיר would also hold the זב liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's exemption covered tools like a needle stuck in clothing, which people normally carry in their hand. A זב's pouch is always worn this way, so this is its normal way of being carried. In that case even רבי מאיר agrees there is a full act of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: Say that you heard him. It grants a limited point in order to deny a wider one.
Its usual way, meaning the normal manner of doing the action.
A thing or object.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'usual way.' In step 16, the issue was whether the worker's own habit counts. Here, אביי points out that the pouch's usual way is simply how everyone carries it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
say that you heard Rabbi Meir rule this way
regarding a thing for which this is not its usual way;
but regarding a thing for which this is its usual way,
did you hear him say so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the exempt ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's exemption only covers an unusual way of carrying. The pouch is always carried this way, so even רבי מאיר would hold the זב liable.

steps.title: Proof from a הדיוט Who Carves a קב in Wood
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves his point: a הדיוט who carves a קב-sized hollow in wood is surely liable, even though he does not work like a craftsman.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, then a layman who carved out a קב in a piece of wood on Shabbat would also not be liable according to רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his challenge with a clear example. A non-professional doing a מלאכה in his own normal way is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדיוט cannot carve like a professional, but this is the normal way for him to do it. If רבי מאיר exempted everything that differs from a craftsman's method, this layman would be exempt too. That result is obviously wrong, so the 'normal way' of an act depends on the case.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so. It introduces a proof by showing an absurd result.
A layman, someone who is not a professional craftsman.
A unit of volume. Here it means a hollow of that size carved out as a vessel.
A split piece of wood.

phrases.english: for if you do not say so,
then according to this, a layman
who carved out a kav in a piece of wood on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא מְחַיַּיב?
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Meir, would he also not be liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's challenge in step 19 with a case whose result is obviously wrong.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that רבי מאיר exempts only acts that are unusual for that object or person, not acts done in their normal way.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a הדיוט carving a קב in wood on שבת, who is obviously liable.

steps.title: רב המנונא: A זב of Two Sightings vs. a זב of Three
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא gives a new answer. The liable ברייתא is about a זב with two sightings, and the exempt ברייתא is about a זב with three sightings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב המנונא said: It is not difficult. Here it is a זב with two sightings; there it is a זב with three sightings.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב יוסף's answer was rejected, רב המנונא offers a different answer. He says the two ברייתות are talking about two different kinds of זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב with two sightings needs the pouch to see whether a third sighting happens, because that would make him owe a קרבן. So the pouch matters, and carrying it is liable. A זב who already had three sightings seems to gain nothing from the pouch, so carrying it is only פטור אבל אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It shows that the previous answer is dropped.
A man with an unusual discharge that makes him ritually impure.
Sightings, meaning occurrences of the discharge.
Here... there. It splits the two sources into two different cases.

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer shifts from a מחלוקת between תנאים to a difference between cases. Both ברייתות can now agree with each other.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Hamnuna said: it is not difficult:
here it is about a zav who had two sightings,
there it is about a zav who had three sightings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a new answer to step 17's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into two different cases (תרי גווני).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to discuss the same זב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liable: a זב with two sightings, who needs the pouch for checking. Exempt: a זב with three sightings, for whom the pouch seems pointless.

steps.title: A זב of Three Sightings Still Needs the Pouch for Counting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a זב with three sightings also needs the pouch, to check that his seven clean days really are clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a זב of two sightings, who is liable because he needs the pouch for checking? A זב of three also needs it, for counting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב המנונא's split. It argues that the pouch is useful to both kinds of זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To become pure, a זב must count seven clean days with no discharge. The pouch helps him know whether a day was clean. So even a זב with three sightings has a real use for the pouch, and he should also be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It challenges a distinction between two cases.
Checking, meaning examining whether a discharge happened.
Counting the seven clean days a זב needs for purification.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת דְּחַיָּיב,
phrases.english: What is different about a zav with two sightings, who is liable,
because he needs the pouch for checking?
A zav with three sightings also
needs it for counting!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת דְּחַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction רב המנונא drew in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's claim that a זב with three sightings has no use for the pouch.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זב with three sightings must still count seven clean days, so the pouch is useful to him and carrying it should be liable.

steps.title: The Exempt Case Is the Day of the Third Sighting
steps.stepSummary: The exempt ברייתא only refers to the same day the third sighting happened. That day can never count as a clean day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was only needed for that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It narrows the exempt ברייתא to the day the זב saw his third discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the day of the third sighting, the counting of clean days cannot begin, and his קרבן is already required. So on that day the pouch truly has no use for him. That is why carrying it is only פטור אבל אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for... It narrows a source to a specific case.
That same day.

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's split between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה was rejected, because the pouch is always carried that way. Under רב המנונא's answer, a זב who carries his pouch is liable when he has had two sightings, since he needs it for checking. He is exempt only on the day of his third sighting, when the pouch serves no halachic purpose. The next steps deal with its practical use of keeping his clothes clean.

phrases.english: It was only needed for that same day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 22 and saves רב המנונא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the exempt ברייתא to a specific time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A זב with three sightings always needs the pouch for his clean-day counting.
steps.terutzMaskana: On the day of the third sighting itself, counting cannot happen, so the pouch is useless and he is exempt.

steps.title: The pouch still keeps his clothes clean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 23: even on the day of the third sighting, the זב needs the pouch so his clothes do not get dirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he still needs the pouch so that his clothes will not get dirty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. Even if the pouch is useless for checking clean days, it still has a practical use: it keeps his clothes clean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 tried to show that on the day of the third sighting the pouch has no use, so carrying it would not make one liable. The challenge says the pouch still has a use, a practical one. If it has a use, why should carrying it be exempt?

keyTerms.meaning: will become dirty / soiled
his clothes (literally 'his garments')
he needs it

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about a halachic use. The גמרא already agreed there is none on that day. It is pointing to a purely practical use, which is keeping clothes clean.

phrases.english: But doesn't he need it
so that his clothes will not get dirty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 23 that the pouch is useless on the day of the third sighting.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 23 that the pouch has no purpose on the day of the third sighting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pouch still has a practical purpose, which is protecting his clothes from dirt. That should make it count as a needed object.

steps.title: This תנא holds that preventing dirt is not a real purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the תנא of the exempt ברייתא holds that using something only to prevent dirt does not count as a significant purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: This תנא is the one who holds that any use meant only to prevent dirt is not considered important.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. The author of the exempt ברייתא holds that keeping things clean is not a 'real' use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deny that the pouch keeps his clothes clean. It says that, according to this תנא, a use that only prevents dirt does not count halachically. So on that day the pouch is still treated as having no real purpose, and carrying it is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה/ברייתא era; here, the author of the ברייתא
saving from dirt / preventing filth
is not considered significant

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule: a purpose of merely preventing dirt may not give an object halachic importance. רבי זירא will show this rule appears elsewhere.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
This tanna is the one who said
that any use to prevent dirt
is not considered significant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the תנא's view: the practical use is real, but this תנא does not count it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Keeping clothes clean is a real use, so the pouch is needed and carrying it should make one liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: For this תנא, preventing dirt is not a significant use, so the pouch still counts as having no purpose on that day.

steps.title: Source: the bowl turned over on the wall
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא begins quoting a משנה to show that a תנא holds that preventing dirt is not a significant purpose. The case is a bowl placed upside down on a wall in the rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone turns a bowl upside down on a wall. If he did it so the bowl would get rinsed by the rain, the water has the status of 'כי יותן' (it makes food able to become טמא). If he did it so... [continues on the next amud].
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings proof that there is a תנא who holds this view. He starts quoting a משנה. This passage stops in the middle, just as the משנה reaches the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of 'כי יותן', water only makes food able to become טמא if the person wanted that water. If he put the bowl out so it would be rinsed, he wanted the water, so it counts. The second case, which comes next, will be about putting the bowl out only to protect the wall from damage. There the water will not count, which is the proof for רבי זירא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
one who turns a bowl upside down
wall
so that it will be rinsed
'if [water] be placed' (ויקרא 11:38): wanted water that makes food able to receive טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: 'כי יותן' is not about Shabbat. It is a rule of טומאה: food can only become טמא after it gets wet with water the owner wanted. The גמרא borrows the idea of 'what counts as wanting' to explain the Shabbat case.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
One who turns a bowl upside down on the wall,
if it was so that the bowl would be rinsed,
that is under 'If water be placed.'
phrases.notes: The water counts as wanted, so it can make produce susceptible to טומאה

phrases.english: If it was so that...
phrases.notes: The משנה continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבי זירא's claim in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That a תנא holds that preventing dirt or damage is not a significant purpose
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a bowl turned over on a wall in the rain (מכשירין)
